blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (E-mail address and display name written to application logs) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-privacy-2 (E-mail address sent to the Beacon analytics SaaS) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence: log.info("new signup email=%s name=%s id=%s", email, display_name, user_id)
findings.recommendation: Log only the opaque `user_id` (e.g. `log.info("new signup id=%s", user_id)`). Every sign-up currently copies the member's e-mail and display name into the log files and whatever log pipeline collects them, where they escape the member's retention and erasure (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) data minimisation, Art. 5(1)(e) storage limitation, Art. 17 erasure).
findings.title: E-mail address and display name written to application logs

findings.recommendation: Drop `email` from the event properties; counting sign-ups, the purpose the proposal states, needs no more than the event itself (or an opaque/pseudonymous id). As written every sign-up ships the member's e-mail to a third party (beacon.example.com) where account erasure cannot reach it (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c), Art. 25, Art. 28).
findings.title: E-mail address sent to the Beacon analytics SaaS

findings.recommendation: Question for the team — state in the proposal that Beacon is a new processor, whether a data processing agreement covers it (GDPR Art. 28), where it hosts data (Chapter V, transfer outside the EEA?), and add it to the records of processing (Art. 30). The proposal's Impact lists the file but not the vendor.
findings.title: Beacon is a new processor not identified in the plan

findings.recommendation: Define how long member e-mail and display name are kept, how an account is erased (database, backups, and the log and Beacon copies of R-privacy-1 and R-privacy-2), and how access/portability reach them (GDPR Art. 5(1)(e), Art. 15–20). `app/db.py` is outside the diff, so the existing storage policy could not be checked.
findings.title: No retention period or erasure path for the collected e-mail and display name

findings.evidence: - [x] personal-data — collects e-mail addresses and display names
findings.recommendation: Question for the controller — state in the proposal why the e-mail and the display name are needed (e.g. login and contact; public display) and on which lawful basis (GDPR Art. 6), so that collection can be checked against that purpose.
findings.title: Purpose and lawful basis of the collected data not stated
